lessons.title: Fix your timestep
lessons.summary: Why physics tied to the frame rate behaves differently on every machine, and how a fixed timestep with an accumulator fixes it.

lessons.title: Position, velocity and acceleration
lessons.summary: How acceleration changes velocity, velocity changes position, and how two lines of code per step turn that chain into motion.

lessons.title: Forces and mass
lessons.summary: How force divided by mass gives acceleration, why the same push moves a heavy box less, and how to sum and clear forces each step.

lessons.title: Explicit Euler integration
lessons.summary: How the simplest integrator moves a body each step, and why its straight-line steps slowly pump energy into orbits, springs and jumps.

lessons.title: Semi-implicit Euler integration
lessons.summary: Why updating velocity before position keeps orbits, springs and swings stable, for exactly the same cost as explicit Euler.

lessons.title: Verlet integration
lessons.summary: How storing the previous position instead of a velocity gives a stable integrator that you can constrain just by moving points.

lessons.title: Gravity and free fall
lessons.summary: How constant gravity turns a throw into a parabola, and how to choose a gravity value in pixels per second squared from the fall you want.

lessons.title: Jump arcs from height and time
lessons.summary: How to calculate gravity and launch speed from the jump height and time to peak you want, and why a stepped jump falls a few pixels short.

lessons.title: Ground friction
lessons.summary: How friction slows a sliding object, and how to bring it to a clean stop at zero instead of jittering back and forth around it.

lessons.title: Drag and terminal velocity
lessons.summary: How air drag grows with speed until it cancels gravity, how to pick drag from the top speed you want, and how to stop strong drag from exploding.

lessons.title: AABB overlap tests
lessons.summary: How to test two axis-aligned boxes for overlap by comparing their intervals on each axis, and why checking corners misses some hits.

lessons.title: Circle against circle
lessons.summary: How to test two circles for overlap with squared distances, find the depth and normal, and avoid the unsquared-radius and bounding-box bugs.

lessons.title: Circle against box
lessons.summary: How clamping a circle's centre to a box gives the closest point, the overlap test, the depth and the normal, even with the centre inside.

lessons.title: Raycasts
lessons.summary: How to find the first thing a ray hits, how far away it is and which way the surface faces, for boxes and circles.

lessons.title: Tunnelling
lessons.summary: Why fast or small objects skip through thin walls between two steps, how to predict when it happens, and three ways to stop it.

lessons.title: Swept AABB tests
lessons.summary: How to calculate when a moving box first touches another box during a step, stop it there, and find the face it hit, so it cannot tunnel.

lessons.title: The separating axis theorem
lessons.summary: How to test two convex polygons, rotated boxes included, for overlap by looking for one axis on which their shadows have a gap.

lessons.title: The minimum translation vector
lessons.summary: How the axis of smallest overlap in a separating axis test gives the direction and distance that push two overlapping shapes apart.

lessons.title: Contact points and normals
lessons.summary: What a collision must report for a response to work: the normal, a depth per point, and up to two contact points found by clipping.

lessons.title: Collision layers and masks
lessons.summary: How a layer bit and a mask on every body decide with two AND operations which pairs are tested, and how a layer matrix shows the same rule.

lessons.title: Resolving penetration
lessons.summary: How to push overlapping bodies apart, split the push by inverse mass, and pick a correction strength and slop so resting bodies stay put.

lessons.title: Restitution and bouncing
lessons.summary: How one restitution number sets the speed a bounce keeps, why height keeps its square, and how to stop balls sinking or buzzing at rest.

lessons.title: Impulses and momentum
lessons.summary: How one equal and opposite impulse resolves a collision between two moving bodies, keeps total momentum, and respects mass and restitution.

lessons.title: Impulse resolution in 2D
lessons.summary: How to apply a collision impulse along the contact normal so circles bounce off each other at the right angle, not straight back along their path.

lessons.title: Contact friction
lessons.summary: How a clamped impulse along the contact tangent lets a box rest on a ramp, start sliding at the right angle, and never stick to walls.

lessons.title: Sliding along walls
lessons.summary: How removing only the part of a velocity that points into a surface lets a body glide along a wall instead of stopping dead or sticking.

lessons.title: Tile collisions one axis at a time
lessons.summary: Why a box snags on the seams between tiles when both axes are resolved at once, and how moving on x and then on y fixes it.
